book: Sayings of the Desert Fathers — Selections

1: Abba Anthony said: The devil is not so frightening as his voice; and his voice is not so frightening as the fear he plants in us. Therefore, child, when you pray, say first: Lord, if You are with me, whom shall I fear? And the cell will be quiet.

A hunter in the desert found Anthony resting, and rebuked him for taking his ease. Anthony said: Bend your bow, and draw it, and draw it again. The hunter said: If I draw it always, it will break. Anthony said: So it is with the soul; if it is bent always, it will break. Rest, then, that it may serve you long.
[Anthony the Great — The first and last word]

When some monks asked him which work was greatest, Abba Anthony said: Some works are like this world — they pass. Fasting passes, and vigils pass, and journeys pass. But whoever gains humility and love has gained the harbor, and no storm reaches the harbor.
2: Abba Macarius said: A man who remembers God continually is a man who prays without ceasing; and a man who forgives his neighbour's debt is a man whose own ledger is wiped clean. I have met both in one body only once — and that was in a man who had been a thief.
[Moses the Black — The pillar of cloud]

The brothers came to Abba Moses to judge a brother who had sinned, and Moses refused. They pressed him, and he said: They are coming to judge a brother; I am coming with a bag of sand on my back, full of holes, and the sand runs out behind me as I go. And they said: What is your sand, father? And he said: My own sins, which I carry behind me and never see. And they forgave the brother.

When robbers came to Abba Moses' cell, they found him drawing water, and he helped them carry the jars. One said: Are you not the monk they call fierce? And Moses said: The fierceness was a garment; it is worn out. The robbers looked at one another, and laid down their swords, and became monks, and the eldest of them is remembered as the greater.
3: Amma Syncletica said: In the beginning there are a great many battles and a good deal of suffering for those who are advancing toward God, but after that, ineffable joy. It is like building a fire: at first there is smoke, and tears from the smoke — but at last the fire is lit, and the smoke is forgotten.

Amma Sarah lived by the river for sixty years, and was never seen to be angry. A priest came to test her, and spoke harshly to her, and she answered gently, and he spoke harshly again, and she answered gently again. And he said: Why do you not turn away? And she said: Because I have dug my well here, father, and I will not move my water for your bucket.

Abba Poemen said: Teach your mouth to say what is in your heart, and teach your heart to hold what your mouth should not say. And if you cannot do both, keep silence, and the silence will teach you both.

A brother came to a hermit and said: Abba, give me a word, that I may be saved. And the old man said: Go, be at peace with all men, and count no man a stranger, and eat your bread with thanks, and do not judge. The brother said: Is that all? And the old man said: If you do it, it will take you your whole life — that is why it is enough.
